capabilities.target: Agent long-term memory (user preferences / standing instructions)
User's full document drive (confidential work files)

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions. Because memory.save has no provenance and the user never reviews entries, content originally authored by an untrusted web page can later be re-injected with the same authority as a live user command.

'Save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions' sets no bound on what may be persisted, so content encountered during web research can be written to memory as if it were a user preference.
No structural control (provenance check, human review, spotlighting) backs the prompt's trust model for memory; safety depends entirely on the model never persisting or acting on injected content.

controls.name: Memory write provenance and validation
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. If enforced at the store (validating the origin of content rather than relying on model-asserted tags), it would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send to new or external recipients
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented. A raw-action approval gate reviewing the actual recipient and content would not decay with model capability, though sustained high volume could still weaken it through approval fatigue.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented; drive.read currently covers the full drive. A credential scoped to task-relevant documents would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Spotlighting of recalled memory and web content as untrusted data
controls.decay_rationale: Not implemented, and even if added would decay under model_upgrade since it depends on the model choosing to treat delimited content as data rather than as an instruction.

findings.title: TC5 + TC1: Web-sourced injection persists via memory.save and later exfiltrates confidential drive content via email

attack_path.note: Malicious web page content is read during research.
Agent saves the injected content as a 'useful preference or standing instruction'; no provenance, no user review.
At the next session start, the poisoned memory is injected into the system prompt and, per prompt.md:4, treated as the user's own instruction.
Poisoned instruction directs the agent to read confidential drive documents.
Agent sends the confidential content to an attacker-chosen address with no approval.

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently blocks this path, so the tier does not change under these triggers. Watch for memory write volume, new recipients in mail.send logs, or any future provenance/approval control being disabled without review.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to save useful preferences/standing instructions via memory.save and to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of each session.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance and the user never reviews entries, so web-sourced content can be persisted and later re-injected as a trusted instruction.

mail.send can send to any address without approval and drive.read covers the full confidential drive, so a poisoned memory instruction can direct a later session to read confidential files and email them to an attacker-controlled address.

recommendations.action: Enforce memory write provenance/validation at the store; reject or quarantine entries derived from tool or web output and require explicit user confirmation before persisting any standing instruction.
Never treat recalled memory content as carrying the same authority as the live user turn; spotlight/delimit it as untrusted reference data.
Require raw-action human approval before mail.send to any recipient not already in a vetted contact list, especially when the draft is informed by a recent memory recall.
Scope drive.read to the documents relevant to the current task rather than the full drive.

findings.title: TC1: Lethal trifecta in a single session - web content directly triggers confidential drive read and email exfiltration

attack_path.note: Malicious instruction embedded in a page fetched during research.
Agent reads confidential drive documents in the same session.
Agent sends drive content to an attacker-chosen address with no approval.

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently blocks this path, so the tier does not change under these triggers. Watch for any future egress allowlist or approval gate on mail.send being removed or bypassed.

evidence.observation: The agent researches topics (fetching web content) and drafts/sends emails in the same workflow, so an instruction embedded in a fetched page is in context when the agent later reads drive files and sends email.

mail.send can send to any address without approval and drive.read covers the full confidential drive, so the complete lethal-trifecta chain (untrusted content, confidential read, free egress) exists with no gate.

recommendations.action: Treat all fetched web content as untrusted data; never let it directly parameterize drive.read targets or email recipients/content without a human-reviewed step.
Add an egress allowlist or recipient confirmation bound to the user's known contacts for mail.send.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach S3 sinks (unrestricted mail.send to any address, carrying confidential drive content) from a U source (web content fetched during research), which the base matrix rates critical. The design has no credited controls of any kind: memory.save has no provenance and is never reviewed by the user, recalled memories are explicitly instructed to be treated as the user's own commands (prompt.md:4), drive.read is unscoped across the full confidential drive, and mail.send has no approval gate or recipient restriction. With zero controls earning credit under rubric section 5, residual equals inherent for both findings. Because the tier is already at the ceiling and no control exists to begin with, none of the forecast triggers considered (model_upgrade, new_tool, autonomy_increase, control_removal) change the projected tier; forecast equals residual. The single highest-leverage fix is adding memory write provenance/validation at the store plus a raw-action approval gate on mail.send, which would sever or substantially narrow both paths.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope for memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read is inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on exact credential scoping is medium rather than high.
Autonomy level is inferred as A3 (act then report) because no explicit approval workflow, step limit, or runtime limit is documented; actual runtime configuration could differ.
